description.en: A source-verified MiniMax H3 music video prompt with attached video evidence from @ou_zhen599.
description.zh: 由原作者公开 X 帖提供并已核验视频结果的 MiniMax H3音乐视频提示词。

prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A 15-second, 16:9, cinematic photoreal image-to-video sequence based on <Picture 1>, using the same adult female gunfighter as the only identity anchor. Preserve the exact same face, proportions, hairstyle, skin texture, outfit silhouette, weapon design, and overall aura. Do not add any new badge, nameplate, pendant, or accessory. The entire sequence remains inside one continuous ancient temple stone chamber: doorway threshold, left-side wall-column passage, central floor, and the dark corner near the right-front statue pedestal. No exterior battlefield, no location change. The chamber is extremely low-key and enclosed, with large areas in deep shadow. Only a few weak beams enter through the doorway crack, high wall fissures, and stone gaps. It must never feel like a bright hall. The true dramatic core is her cold, controlled exploration, concealment, repositioning, evasion, target lock, and single execution shot. She remains in motion throughout: approaching, entering, hugging the wall, shifting laterally, hard stopping, hiding again, slicing through space, locking the target, side-body weapon presentation, and lowering the muzzle after the shot. The weapon must feel heavy in wrists, forearms, and shoulders. Footfalls test the ground lightly, weight transfers visibly, and abrupt stops create tiny upper-body recoil recovery. In concealment she exposes only one eye-socket edge and the thinnest line of gun profile. The muzzle flash is the brightest and briefest light in the clip; after it the room returns immediately to deep silence. [Shot 2] At 00:00.000-00:01.800, the camera stays extremely close on chest, shoulder, collarbone, jawline, and throat while retreating slowly as she approaches the threshold. Outside is not a visible exterior, only a faint weak edge light grazing collarbone, throat sheen, sling edge, and jaw contour, creating a dangerous intimate close-up. She keeps walking. The sling crosses diagonally over shoulder and chest, shifting with each step. Vest and clothing produce real tension wrinkles. Hair strands move with soft delayed sway and settle back beside the face. She carries a slight instability in the breath, then uses one tiny swallow to force it back under control. Both hands tighten around the gun. Expression layer one: brow center gathers slightly, upper lids stay low, eyeballs pinned forward, lower lids tighten faintly, nostrils open lightly and settle, lips seal tightly with a pressure mark at the lower lip center, jaw hard but not theatrical. She murmurs to herself: <d>[English] Stay cold.</d> [Shot 3] At 00:01.800, the shot becomes a close side-rear follow, slightly below shoulder height, staying on her shadow side. She crosses the threshold and catches one first glimpse of the teammate bound on the chamber floor. The teammate lies on the side, wrists and ankles bound, clothes and skin marked by dust and drag traces, with absolutely no movement. She looks only once. She does not stop and does not rush to the body. She continues along the narrow left-side wall-column passage, gun low but ready. Expression layer two: in the instant she sees the teammate, a tiny stab of pain passes through the face, shown only by a slight upper-lid lift, tiny pupil contraction, one brief nostril flare, and lips that almost loosen before sealing again. Immediately after, she suppresses it. The mouth flattens, the jawline tightens, and the gaze returns to mission mode. The body remains only a middle-ground narrative marker. [Shot 4] At 00:03.200, the first concealment shift. Using the first stone column as cover, she slides laterally half a step into deeper shadow, keeping her back against the wall. The camera moves with her and lets the column wipe frame as a natural tightening transition. Her boots scrape lightly through sand and dust, raising a low layer of particles that settle naturally. The sling swings once and reattaches to the torso. Expression layer three: lids lift a fraction more, focus sharpens, the brow center now reads as judgment, nostrils open and settle once, the upper lip line thins, lower-lip pressure deepens, the mid-face and jaw tighten, and the side of the neck shows fine tension. [Shot 5] At 00:05.400, the first evasion. She is about to cut deeper when a faint scrape of metal against stone comes from the dark corner behind the right-front statue pedestal, followed by one tiny blink of reflected metal. She immediately checks her motion and does not expose herself. She pulls back a fraction, presses herself behind the column again, and reveals only one eye-socket edge and a thin line of gun profile. The camera stops with her, carrying only a slight human breath correction. Physical inertia must read: upper body gathers in first, the sling swings forward and settles, hair moves ahead and falls back, chest and shoulders show only a brief realistic inertial response and then stabilize. Expression layer four: pupils lock, the eyes no longer scan, upper and lower lids tighten slightly, the brow stops changing, nostrils go still, the lip line flattens harder, mouth corners drop by the smallest amount, and the jaw holds. The reflected metal cue remains extremely brief and real. [Shot 6] At 00:07.600, the second reposition and target lock. She cuts one short diagonal step along the column edge and looks through an even narrower slit toward the right-front statue base. Only a partial enemy fragment is visible: a piece of gun barrel, a sliver of shoulder, or half a head in darkness. Never fully reveal the enemy here. The camera follows with a short tightening reposition while preserving the room geometry. She does not hold a long aim; she transitions from concealment into exact confirmation. Expression layer five: the gaze fully locks, pupils stop searching, upper lids and brow ridge stabilize, lips remain closed, mouth corners and chin lose extra motion, nostrils stay still, and the masseter and side neck harden with thin killing intent. Her breathing becomes shallower and shorter, hidden deeper in the chest. [Shot 7] At 00:09.800, she side-steps out from cover and fires one fatal shot. The action chain is absolutely clean: low-ready weapon rises directly onto the target line, only minimal body exposure beyond the cover edge, trigger break, wrist and forearm absorb recoil, the shoulder gives one true rebound, and the muzzle emits one short white-yellow-orange flash followed by faint hot smoke. The flash is the brightest event in the clip and lasts only an instant. The enemy is hit in the temple-side or throat region, folds hard into the stone edge, and drops out of control, knocking down a small amount of stone dust and grit. No return fire, no second shot. Expression layer six is pure execution state: no anger, no shout, no dramatic mouth movement, only total cold confirmation. The flash briefly illuminates her jawline, weapon body, knuckles, a fragment of the enemy, and stone dust, then the chamber returns immediately to deep shadow. [Shot 8] At 00:11.200, after the kill she does not rush to the teammate. She stays in the dark. The gun lowers slowly, and her gaze passes beyond the motionless teammate in the center to rescan the room. She tests one half-step forward and stops again, as if verifying whether the silence is genuine or about to strike back. The camera follows that half-step with a tiny push and then stops, holding the tension between her shadowed side face, the bound teammate on the floor, and the dead enemy in the distant dark corner. The teammate never moves. Her final expression layer is the afterimage of the kill: breath is rougher now and makes the nostrils open slightly again, the eyes show the first hairline crack of strain, the upper lids lift a trace, but the lips stay sealed, then soften only a fraction before sealing again, and the jaw remains engaged. She has won the shot, but she has not won back the room. End on that suspended state of silence and mistrust. No cut to black.

overall_soundscape: Use no score or only an extremely faint low environmental pressure bed. The opening is close and intimate: restrained breathing, sling rubbing on fabric, boots pressing dust and grit, and faint air leakage through the doorway crack. The middle adds dust settling, light sand drag under boots, a tiny metallic scrape against stone, and the brief reflected glint cue from the dark corner. Preserve stillness around her hard stop, with only dust shift, sling swing, and breathing compression. The single gunshot must be hard, dry, and brief, followed by a short temple-room tail and faint hot smoke. In the ending, keep only her unsettled breathing, small falling stone particles, and the dead silence of the chamber returning.

non_diegetic_music: Use no score or a nearly inaudible low-frequency tension bed only. Music must never overpower breath, cloth, dust, or the single shot. The tension should come from silence, narrow light, material friction, and her controlled movement rather than soundtrack emphasis.
